lines: Master, please be at ease and hold on to Tokiko's back.
As Tokiko kneeled down for him, Kotaro clambered up onto her backside.
Even heavier than that weight, the future of the Fuma rested profoundly on Tokiko's back.
There's nothing to be afraid of. You can fall asleep there if you like.
I-I'm alright. I'm not scared when you're with me, Tokiko.
His face as she looked back over her shoulder had been trying hard to hide his fright.
That is why you are the master of the Fuma.
Tokiko smiled gently and stood up.
Tokiko broke into a dash as quick as the wind.
She moved as fast as she could to break through the Igawa's siege, and to leave the burning Fuma residence behind.
There were only a few Fuma shinobi left remaining to accompany them.
There they are!! It's the Fuma!!
The flames of the manor behind them made their figures stand out in the darkness.
Relying on their numbers, the Igawa shinobi narrowed the encirclement.
We entrust the master to you!
Without a moment's hesitation, Tokiko had let her subordinates take her place.
Though they were outnumbered, and each knew the fate that awaited them...
Without showing an ounce of fear, they leapt into the crowd of enemies.
But their pursuers relentlessly cornered them.
Fire! Use fire!! Set the forest on fire and flush them out!!
Bastards! You fools have no idea what true Fire Art is!! Let's go, Iwamaru!
That's right, Kagaribi!! Let's give them a taste of the true essence of the Fuma Jutsu!
They shouted loudly and daringly cut their way through the enemy in order to intentionally draw their focus.
One by one, the Fuma ninja were falling.
They used themselves as shields to stall the enemy, or were engaged in small skirmishes during the whirlwind of their escape.
All in order to protect the lord of the Fuma, their only link to the future of the clan.
By the time they'd escaped to the safety of the village shrine's grove, Tokiko and Kotaro had no friends left by their side.
Master, please take a brief rest here.
Tokiko let Kotaro down, who had been clinging to her back as if he were glued to it.
The moment she felt that weight lift from her...
Tokiko almost fell to her knees on the spot as a powerful dizziness struck her.
I-I'm alright. I'm just a little out of breath.
Tokiko smiled calmly, not faulting Kotaro for having called her "big sister."
But you're okay, right? You didn't get hit somewhere?
Please don't worry. I haven't been injured.
I will not lie to you, master. Come, let us rest a little.
Tokiko sat him down, then she took her seat by his side to guard him.
For the time being, they had managed to break through the enemies encircling the Fuma residence.
The burning glow of the flames still lit the sky in the direction of the residence, however, those flames had yet to reach this grove where the village shrine was located.
And yet, they were in no position to relax their guard.
After escaping into the forest and allowing the young Kotaro to rest, Tokiko was able to breathe a sigh of relief, but the enemy was expanding its search.
Enemy pursuit squads were closing in from all directions.
As proof, the flames of torches held by their pursuers had been flickering here and there in the deep dark forest.
The swaying flames made it seem as if Will-o'-wisps were searching for them instead of people.
Kotaro was looking up at Tokiko anxiously.
His tiny body trembled in short shivers.
Then please come here and let me warm you.
Kotaro jumped into her chest the moment Tokiko held out her arms.
Tokiko embraced him as tightly as she could. He was still so small and yet that tiny frame carried the future of the Fuma Clan.
Within that embrace, Kotaro's trembling eventually subsided.
(There are still those fighting back in the village. We must join up with them...)
Even then, the sounds of battle could be heard constantly from all over the town.
Unless they somehow joined up with their allies, she had no hope of getting Kotaro out of Fuma Village.
Master... Please do not leave my side...
The young head of the family nodded wordlessly, then released his grip on her.
I'm alright now. I'm not cold anymore.
A tear had streaked down Tokiko's chest, but she pretended not to notice it.
Despite this harsh situation, Kotaro was doing a surprising job of keeping his composure so as not to be a burden to Tokiko.
But it was a desperate actーone as the head of the Fuma.
(I must protect this child, no matter what happens.)
(Even if it costs me my life.)
Like her subordinates who had been cast down before her, Tokiko once again strengthened that grim resolve within her.
But as if to mock that resolve, an enemy presence was rapidly approaching.
It's just that head brat and one other!!
You Igawa scum!! Come at me!!
